formula.zh-TW: 營業成本 ÷ 營業收入

meaning.zh-TW: 這一期賣出去的商品本身的成本，等於期初存貨加本期進貨減期末存貨；還沒賣掉的部分留在存貨裡，不算成本。
meaning.en: The cost of the goods actually sold this period, opening inventories plus purchases minus closing inventories; what is still unsold stays in inventories and is not a cost yet.

meaning.zh-TW: 損益表第一列，這一期本業收進來的金額，當分母表示「每做一元生意」。
meaning.en: The first line of the income statement, what the core business brought in this period; as the denominator it means ‘for each unit of sales’.

example.zh-TW: 一家自行車零件批發商這一年營業收入 {{money:5000000}}，營業成本 {{money:3200000}}：{{money:3200000}} ÷ {{money:5000000}} ＝ {{percent:0.64|digits=0}}。意思是每賣 {{money:100}} 的貨，有 {{money:64}} 是貨本身的成本；同一家公司的毛利率就是 1 − {{percent:0.64|digits=0}} ＝ {{percent:0.36|digits=0}}。數字是網站自己編的，不是真實公司。
example.en: A bicycle parts wholesaler has revenue of {{money:5000000}} this year and cost of sales of {{money:3200000}}: {{money:3200000}} ÷ {{money:5000000}} = {{percent:0.64|digits=0}}. For every {{money:100}} of goods sold, {{money:64}} is the cost of the goods themselves; the same company’s gross margin is simply 1 − {{percent:0.64|digits=0}} = {{percent:0.36|digits=0}}. The figures are made up for the site, not a real company.

reading.zh-TW: 成本率越高，表示賣出去的東西本身越貴、留下的毛利越薄；它和毛利率是一體兩面，兩個加起來一定是 {{percent:1|digits=0}}，所以看法和毛利率相同，只是方向相反。它要和同業比，批發與量販成本率天生很高，不代表經營不好；看自己的趨勢時，成本率上升可能是進貨變貴、也可能是為了搶市場而降價，分子分母要分開看。有一個會讓它失真的地方：營業成本是用期初存貨加進貨減期末存貨倒算出來的，期末盤點多出來的存貨會沖減營業成本，成本率就跟著下降，那不是真的變賺錢。常見誤讀：把銷管費用也算進成本率，銷管費用是毛利之後才扣的營業費用，另外有銷售及管理費用率在看它，成本率只看賣出商品本身的成本。
reading.en: The higher the cost ratio, the dearer the goods sold and the thinner the gross profit left; it is the mirror image of the gross margin, the two always add up to {{percent:1|digits=0}}, so you read it the same way with the sign reversed. Compare with peers: wholesale and mass retail naturally run a high cost ratio and that is not poor management. Over the company’s own trend, a rising ratio may mean dearer purchases or price cuts to win market share, so look at numerator and denominator separately. One thing distorts it: cost of sales is worked out backwards as opening inventories plus purchases minus closing inventories, so a surplus found in the year-end count lowers cost of sales and the ratio falls without the business really earning more. A common misreading is including distribution and administrative expenses in the cost ratio; those are operating expenses deducted after gross profit with their own measure, the selling, general and administrative expense ratio, while the cost ratio looks only at the cost of the goods sold.
